cleanups.note: Duplicate alias collision: 'banana chips' is also an alias of dried-banana-chip. 'banana chips' means dried banana crisps, NOT plantain chips (which own platanitos/tostones). Drop from plantain-chip so the query routes to dried-banana-chip (correct owner); plantain-chip keeps plantain chips/platanitos/tostones.
Duplicate alias: 'caramel popcorn' also lives on caramel-corn, the dedicated child (parentIds=['popcorn-snack']). The specific child should own it; keeping it on the parent splits the match.
Duplicate alias: 'veggie straws' also lives on veggie-straw, the dedicated child (parentIds=['vegetable-chip']). Let the specific child own it; vegetable-chip keeps 'veggie chips'/'vegetable crisps'.

Brand collision: 'cheez-it' also lives on cheese-cracker. Cheez-It IS a cheese cracker, so the specific cheese-cracker item (which also has 'cheez its', 'cheddar cracker') should own it, not the generic 'cracker' umbrella.

Cross-category alias leak (target is the Dairy & Eggs base 'cheese'): a 'cheese cracker' query exact-matches base cheese instead of the Snacks cheese-cracker item. Removing this leak lets 'cheese cracker' resolve to cheese-cracker (NAME match) in Snacks.
